claim: ProShares inverse ETFs (including SH, -1x S&P 500) have a one-day investment objective; for any holding period other than one day, realized return can be higher or lower than the Daily Target because of compounding -- smaller index gains/losses and higher index volatility push returns worse than the Daily Target, while larger index moves and lower volatility push returns better than the Daily Target. ProShares' own guidance: investors should monitor inverse-ETF holdings 'as frequently as daily' and consider a rebalancing strategy, i.e. these instruments are built for short-horizon tactical use, not a static multi-year hedge.
quote: Remember that ProShares inverse ETFs have one-day investment objectives. While they may be held for periods longer than one day, you should monitor your investments as frequently as daily and consider a rebalancing strategy.
limitations: Vendor (issuer) published guidance, not independent peer-reviewed research; no exact publication date on the page itself (fetched_at used as the reference date); does not disclose a specific backtest of a monthly-rebalanced, beta-sized hedge overlay on a factor book (this iteration's exact construction) -- it documents the instrument's general one-day-target compounding property, which this iteration applies to its own hedge construction rather than borrowing a number from the source.
independent_replication: Not independently re-derived here; the compounding/path-dependency mechanism described (return diverges from the simple multi-day inverse due to daily rebalancing) is the same mechanism documented across the broader leveraged/inverse-ETF literature (e.g. Cheng & Madhavan 2009, 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds'), not separately opened this pass.
impact_on_spec: Grounds the direction-review's caveat that the hedged forms (b)/(b') in this iteration use actual SH/PSQ prices (not a synthetic -1x return series) specifically so this decay/tracking-error cost is priced into the result rather than assumed away; a positive diversifier edge, if found, must be interpreted net of this known drag, not as a clean beta hedge.
